hero.caption:
The steamboats Montana and Penguin by the St. Charles Bridge, Missouri, about 1880. The boats are evidently unable to pass under the bridge because of the high water level in the river.
Montana's hull was built at California, Pennsylvania, in 1879 and she was completed at Pittsburgh. One of the largest if not the largest steamer ever to operate on the Missouri River, she was sunk in June 1884 either by hitting a pier of the St. Charles Bridge or a snag beneath it.

Penguin, 61 tons, was built at Burlington, Iowa, in 1877. Converted into a towboat by 1891, she sank after a collision at Evansville in 1907.
